The average size and volume fraction of the γ' phase in the Rene N4 alloy studied are about 0.25μm and 65v/o, respectively.
Slip trace analysis showed that primary cube slip had occurred even at room temperature for the [111] specimens.
The range of orientations exhibiting cube slip expanded with increasing test temperature, until at 980°C only orientations very near the [001] or [011] exhibited octahedral slip.
The critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) for cube slip exhibited a peak near 760°C, similar to the behavior observed for octahedral slip.
Tension-compression anisotropies were observed for both octahedral and cube slip in Rene N4.
The LCP model was able to explain the major deviations from Schmid's law in Rene N4 as being due to the orientation-dependent tension-compression anisotropy.
The effect of the applied stress in promoting cube cross-slip, which would increase the strength of orientations away from the [001], was found to be relatively unimportant in Rene N4.

Analysis of published data for the single-crystal superalloy PWA 1480 showed the same result as Rene N4, with the tension-compression anisotropy term being dominant and the cube cross-slip term being relatively unimportant.

At temperatures above 760°C, which is about the peak strength temperature in Rene N4, deviations from Schmid's law were reduced and the orientation and tension-compression dependencies of yield strength for octahedral slip changed.
For the orientations exhibiting octahedral slip at 980°C, the yield strengths appeared to be somewhat higher in compression than in tension, which was the opposite of the behavior observed at 760°C.
